content.text: The tainted `param` goes through a trivial pass-through (`Test.doSomething`), is concatenated into `fileName`, and used directly in `new java.io.FileOutputStream(new java.io.File(fileName), false)` — no path validation, canonicalization, or allow-listing is performed anywhere in the flow.

input.justification:
User-controlled request parameter "BenchmarkTest01238" flows (via a trivial list add/remove pass-through in the inner Test class, which does not sanitize anything) into fileName = TESTFILES_DIR + bar, which is then used directly to construct a java.io.File / FileOutputStream. There is no validation, canonicalization, or allow-list check on the path component before it reaches the file-creation sink, so an attacker can supply path traversal sequences (e.g. ../../) to write to arbitrary file locations. This matches the classic OWASP Benchmark path-injection pattern and is a true positive.</justification>
